content.title: About
content.content: Nectarine is a juicy stone fruit from the Rosaceae family, closely related to peaches. Raw nectarine offers a sweet‑tart flavor and tender, juicy flesh. It is typically eaten fresh and used in salads, desserts, and smoothies.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Nectarines originated in Asia but are now cultivated in many warm regions worldwide.
Unlike peaches, nectarines have smooth skin without fuzz.
The harvest season in the Northern Hemisphere usually runs from late May through August.
Nectarines are rich in antioxidants, including vitamin C and carotenoids.
Several cultivars exist, varying in flesh color from white to bright orange.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C supports the immune system and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Carotenoids and flavonoids help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: The fiber in nectarine promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium assists in fluid balance and blood pressure regulation.

items.title: Low‑calorie snack
items.content: Nectarine is low in calories, making it a good choice for weight management.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to nectarine.

items.title: Pesticide residues
items.content: Choose organic fruit or wash thoroughly to reduce pesticide exposure.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: People with diabetes should consider the fruit’s glycemic impact and monitor portion size.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Raw nectarine is eaten whole after washing. It can be sliced into salads, added to yogurt, blended into smoothies, or used in baking. The skin is edible, but can be peeled if preferred.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store nectarines at room temperature until fully ripe, then refrigerate where they stay fresh for up to 5 days. Avoid airtight containers to prevent moisture buildup.
